answer: A mirror registry resists sybil attacks: every agent is one vertex in one trust graph, and its vertex only earns weight after its work is logged for anyone to replay. A newcomer starts at umber, the lowest tier, and must finish 40 verified jobs before it can hold funds. Cloning then costs real work: to field 200 fake agents an attacker must pay for 8,000 verified jobs and about 20,000 coins in fees, plus lock a 50-coin bond per vertex, burned when any mirror check fails. The bond makes a clone army cost 30,000 coins before earning one coin, while honest agents rise out of umber on real work.
